cards.prompt: Which of these is not an orchestration framework?
options: LangGraph
CrewAI
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Strands Agents
cards.why: AgentCore hosts and operates agents built with any of the others; it does not define your agent's loop. Treating it as a competitor to LangGraph is the category error interviewers listen for.

cards.prompt: The requirement is 'pause for a partner's approval, which may take days, then resume exactly where it stopped, surviving deployments'. Which favours what?
options: CrewAI, because @human_feedback pauses a Flow
LangGraph, because interrupt() plus a Postgres checkpointer gives durable mid-node pause and resume
AgentCore alone, because sessions last 8 hours
A plain workflow, because approvals are deterministic
cards.why: This is the durability one-liner in action. CrewAI's persistence is step-level and 8-hour sessions are far shorter than 'days'; AgentCore would host the LangGraph graph, not replace it.

cards.prompt: Choosing CrewAI means you cannot deploy on AgentCore.
cards.why: AgentCore is framework-agnostic and the docs name CrewAI explicitly. Orchestration and platform are independent choices.

cards.prompt: One-liner: LangGraph = control and ___.
cards.why: Control is the explicit graph; durability is checkpointing, interrupts and replay. CrewAI's line is speed and readability; AgentCore's is hosting, identity and ops.

cards.prompt: A partner wants a demo in three days. The job is research, draft, review, in that order, with a two-person team. Which do you pick?
options: LangGraph with a custom StateGraph and PostgresSaver
CrewAI sequential crew, optionally inside a Flow
LangChain create_agent: one ReAct agent holding all three roles' tools
Hand-rolled ReAct loop in boto3
cards.why: Linear roles, small team, speed and readability: CrewAI's sweet spot. LangGraph is viable but you would spend the three days on scaffolding the partner never sees, and one agent with every tool loses the per-role prompts that make the demo readable.

cards.prompt: Strands Agents is AWS's own open-source agent SDK and a legitimate third orchestration option on AgentCore.
cards.why: Strands is model-driven (model, prompt, tools; the model plans) and is the framework AWS's own AgentCore docs and samples lead with, next to LangGraph, Google ADK and OpenAI Agents examples. Knowing it exists signals you have looked at the AWS ecosystem, not just the two popular names.

cards.prompt: The pipeline is OCR, classify, extract five fields, write to the database. Every step is known. What do you use?
options: A supervisor agent so it can adapt
A plain workflow with model calls inside the classify and extract steps; no agent framework needed
CrewAI hierarchical with a manager
LangGraph with interrupt() at each step
cards.why: Known path means a workflow: cheaper, deterministic, auditable. Agent frameworks add loops and cost for flexibility this job does not need; you could still host the workflow on AgentCore if isolation matters.

explain.prompt: Give me your one-liner on LangGraph, CrewAI and AgentCore, and tell me when you would pick each.
explain.modelAnswer:
LangGraph is control and durability: I define the state and the graph explicitly, and I get checkpointing, interrupts and replay. CrewAI is speed and readability: roles and tasks that a partner can read, a working crew in an afternoon, Flows for routing. AgentCore is hosting, identity and ops: not a framework, but the place either of them runs, with per-session microVMs, Gateway for tools, Memory, Identity and traces.

So the choice is two decisions. Platform first: for a Fortune 100 or law-firm client on AWS, AgentCore is usually the answer because their security review asks about isolation, identity and audit, and I would rather not build those.

Then orchestration. LangGraph when there is a human approval step that may take days, when a run is long and must survive restarts, or when I must prove what happened step by step; that is most privileged-document work. CrewAI when the job is a chain of clear roles, the team is small and a readable demo in days matters. And when the path is known up front, neither: a plain pipeline with model calls inside, which I can still host on AgentCore.
rubric: States all three one-liners correctly
Identifies AgentCore as a platform, not a framework; two-dimensional decision
LangGraph criteria: approval, long runs, durability, audit
CrewAI criteria: linear roles, small team, speed and readability
Mentions the plain-workflow option when the path is known

scenarios.situation: A law firm's CTO asks whether the firm should standardise on CrewAI or LangGraph for all future agent work. Two teams already have prototypes, one in each. The firm's main concerns are client confidentiality, auditability and not having to re-platform in a year.
scenarios.question: What do you recommend?

options.text: Standardise on AgentCore as the platform (isolation, identity, observability) and allow both frameworks behind written criteria: LangGraph where approvals or audit of steps are required, CrewAI for linear low-risk assistants.
options.why: The confidentiality and audit concerns live at the platform layer, so that is where standardisation pays off. Framework choice is a per-workload decision and AgentCore makes it reversible.

options.text: Mandate LangGraph everywhere, since privileged-document work will eventually need durable approvals.
options.why: Defensible and consistent, but it slows the low-risk assistants down and still leaves the platform question, where the real confidentiality risk sits, unanswered.

options.text: Pick whichever framework the vendor who demoed last month recommended, and decide hosting later.
options.why: Hosting is where confidentiality and audit are decided; deferring it is deferring the CTO's actual concerns, and a vendor demo is not a selection criterion.

questions.prompt: LangGraph versus CrewAI: which would you choose for us, and why?
questions.modelOutline: Open by reframing: the two solve different problems and neither is the hosting layer, which for this firm is AgentCore. Give the one-liners: LangGraph is control and durability, explicit StateGraph, checkpointers, interrupt() for human approval that can wait days, replayable history; CrewAI is speed and readability, role-based agents and tasks a partner can read, Flows for routing and persistence, native MCP via the mcps field. Then decide for the firm's workload: privileged-document review needs approval gates, survives deployments and must be auditable step by step, so LangGraph for the core review and production agents; CrewAI for low-risk linear assistants such as intake triage or research memos where a readable demo and speed matter. Name the strains honestly: LangGraph is more code; CrewAI's inner loop is opaque, hierarchical mode is non-deterministic, telemetry is on by default. Close with the version context: LangGraph 1.0 since October 2025 with a no-breaking-changes promise, CrewAI 1.x, both hosted unchanged on AgentCore.

questions.prompt: Design an agent platform for a law firm on AWS: isolation, identity, tools, memory and audit. Where does each concern live?
questions.modelOutline: Lay it out by concern. Isolation: AgentCore Runtime, one microVM per runtimeSessionId, destroyed after the session, lifecycle limits set per workload. Identity: inbound JWT from the firm's identity provider so every call is a named associate; outbound per-user OAuth from the Identity vault so the review platform enforces its own permissions; no shared service accounts. Tools: everything behind AgentCore Gateway as MCP, including the firm's own MCP servers, with read tools separated from write tools, Policy rules on which agent may call what, and Guardrails on tool output. Audit: OpenTelemetry traces of every model and tool call to CloudWatch, LangGraph thread history for step-level replay, cost tags per matter. Orchestration: LangGraph for review work with interrupt() before anything leaves the firm; CrewAI for low-risk assistants. Finish with the injection stance: every discovery document is hostile, so least privilege and approval gates are non-negotiable.
